origin_and_geography.native_tract: Bargur hill forest ranges in Anthiyur and Bhavani taluks of Erode district, Tamil Nadu, India
origin_and_geography.agro_climatic_zone: Western semi-arid hilly forest zone, elevation 800m - 1200m
origin_and_geography.historical_background: Bred and maintained primarily by the indigenous Lingayat / Kannada-speaking farming communities of Bargur hills for centuries. Known for their semi-wild husbandry system where herds graze extensively in deep reserve forests.

morphological_traits.horns: Light brown to reddish-brown, medium length, inclined backward, outward, and slightly upward with inward sharp curvature at tips.
morphological_traits.forehead: Prominent, slightly convex with a distinct light brown or reddish central stripe.
morphological_traits.coat_color: Brown with distinct white patches or white with reddish-brown patches; occasionally entirely brown.
morphological_traits.hump_and_dewlap: Moderate compact hump in males; thin, moderate dewlap that does not hinder rapid mountain running.
morphological_traits.body_conformation: Compact, cylindrical body with strong, lean limbs and extremely hard hooves adapted to rocky terrains.

production_and_utility.primary_utility: High-speed draught power and agile hill transport.
production_and_utility.draught_capacity: Unmatched agility, endurance, and speed in hilly and undulating terrains where heavy bullocks cannot operate.

management_and_resilience.diet_and_forage: Naturally sustained on forest undergrowth, indigenous grasses, bamboo leaves, and coarse tree foliage.
management_and_resilience.disease_resistance: Extremely resistant to tick infestations, foot rot, and babesiosis; highly adapted to thrive with minimal veterinary intervention.
management_and_resilience.temperament: Restless, fiery, semi-wild; loyal to their customary handlers but defensive toward strangers.

conservation_status: Vulnerable / Endangered indigenous breed; conservation programs supported by ICAR-NBAGR and TANUVAS.
